tool.name: CRISPRCasTyper
tool.description: detect, annotate and subtype CRISPR-Cas loci
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/cctyper_galaxy.py' --input '$input' --prodigal-mode '$gene_prediction' --workdir cctyper_out --results results #if str($plotting.plot) == 'yes' --plot #end if -- --simplelog -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" $circular --dist $operons.dist --overall_eval $operons.overall_eval --overall_cov_seq $operons.overall_cov_seq --overall_cov_hmm $operons.overall_cov_hmm --ccd $arrays.ccd --pred_prob $arrays.pred_prob --repeat_id $arrays.repeat_id --spacer_id $arrays.spacer_id --spacer_sem $arrays.spacer_sem --repeat_search_backend '$arrays.repeat_search_backend' $arrays.exact_stats $arrays.skip_blast --searchWL $minced.searchWL --minNR $minced.minNR --minRL $minced.minRL --maxRL $minced.maxRL --minSL $minced.minSL --maxSL $minced.maxSL #if str($plotting.plot) == 'no' --no_plot #else --expand $plotting.expand $plotting.no_grid #end if

param.name: input
param.label: Nucleotide sequence(s) to screen
param.help: Genomes, contigs, plasmids or metagenome assemblies. Each sequence is analysed separately.

param.name: gene_prediction
param.label: Gene prediction mode
param.help: pyrodigal needs sequences of at least 20 kb to train a gene model. The automatic mode uses the metagenomic mode when no sequence reaches that length.
param.option: Automatic (single genome, metagenomic for sequences shorter than 20 kb)

param.label: Treat each sequence as circular
param.help: Use for complete circular chromosomes, plasmids and phage genomes.

param.label: Maximum number of unknown genes between Cas genes in an operon
Overall E-value threshold
Overall sequence coverage threshold
Overall HMM coverage threshold

param.name: repeat_search_backend
param.label: Backend for searching known repeats around Cas operons
param.help: BLAST+ is installed together with CRISPRCasTyper and is the fastest option; the bundled search programs need no external program.

param.label: Do not search for CRISPR arrays around Cas operons
param.help: Faster, but arrays that are too degenerate for the array finder are then missed.

param.label: Maximum distance (bp) between a Cas operon and a connected CRISPR array
Probability cut-off for assigning a subtype to a CRISPR repeat
Minimum average repeat identity (%) for a trusted array
Maximum average spacer identity (%) for a trusted array
Maximum standard error of the mean of the spacer lengths for a trusted array
Compute exact repeat and spacer identities
param.help: Slower for large arrays; by default identities are estimated from a sample.

param.label: Search window length
Minimum number of repeats per array
Minimum repeat length
Maximum repeat length
Minimum spacer length
Maximum spacer length

param.name: plot
param.label: Draw a map of the detected loci
param.help: The map is written as vector graphics (SVG) and can be used directly in publications.

param.label: Expand operons by this many bp at both ends
param.help: 0 only fills the gaps between annotated genes. Use e.g. 5000 to show unannotated genes around a locus.

param.label: Do not add a grid to the map

data.name: plot
data.label: ${tool.name} on ${on_string}: map of the detected loci

tool.help:
**What it does**
CRISPRCasTyper detects CRISPR-Cas systems in nucleotide sequences. It
1. predicts genes and searches them against a large collection of Cas HMM profiles, 2. groups Cas genes into operons and predicts the subtype of every operon, 3. finds CRISPR arrays and predicts the subtype associated with their repeat sequence, 4. connects Cas operons and CRISPR arrays into CRISPR-Cas loci, orphan operons and orphan arrays, 5. draws a map of the detected loci.
50 subtypes and variants are covered, from I-A to VI-Y.
-----
**Input**
A nucleotide FASTA file with one or more sequences (draft or complete genomes, contigs, plasmids, phages, metagenome assemblies). Every sequence is analysed on its own, so a multi-contig assembly gives per-contig results.
* *Treat each sequence as circular* is meant for complete circular replicons, and changes how genes are predicted at the sequence ends. * The *gene prediction mode* matters for short input: the gene caller (pyrodigal) needs sequences of at least 20 kb to train a gene model. The default *automatic* mode switches to the metagenomic model when no sequence is that long, which is what you want for plasmids, phages, short contigs and metagenomes.
-----
**Output**
| Output | Content | | ------ | ------- | | CRISPR-Cas loci | One row per CRISPR-Cas locus with the consensus subtype prediction based on both the Cas operon and the adjacent CRISPR arrays, their positions and the individual predictions | | Cas operons | All certain Cas operons with start, end, subtype, module completeness, the Cas genes found and their E-values and HMM/sequence coverages | | CRISPR arrays | All CRISPR arrays with start, end, consensus repeat, number of repeats, repeat/spacer statistics, whether the array is trusted and the subtype predicted from the repeat | | CRISPR arrays (GFF3) | The CRISPR arrays as `repeat_region` features with their repeats (`direct_repeat`) and spacers (`binding_site`) for a genome browser | | map | SVG map of the CRISPR-Cas loci, orphan operons and orphan arrays; interference modules are yellow, adaptation modules blue, Cas6 red, accessory genes purple | | all other output files | A collection with the orphan and putative tables (`cas_operons_orphan`, `cas_operons_putative`, `CRISPR_Cas_putative`, `crisprs_near_cas`, `crisprs_orphan`, `crisprs_putative`), `genes.tab` (all predicted genes), `hmmer.tab` (all HMM hits), `arguments.tab`, the PNG version of the map and one FASTA of spacers per array |
Empty result tables (header only) are written when nothing was found, so the outputs can be used in workflows without special cases. Files that CRISPRCasTyper only produces when there is data are collected in *all other output files*.
-----
**Notes**
* Without any Cas gene hit, CRISPRCasTyper 1.9.0 stops with an internal error instead of reporting an empty result. In that case the tool writes empty result tables and reports a warning, which is the normal outcome for sequences without a CRISPR-Cas system. * cctyper 1.9.0 exits with status 0 on several errors (unreadable input, missing reference files, ...). The wrapper therefore checks that the run reached its last step and fails the job when it did not, and the job output contains the whole CRISPRCasTyper log for diagnostics. * CRISPR arrays are only searched for around Cas operons, so a sequence without Cas genes yields no array calls. * Runtime grows with the number of genes: a bacterial genome takes a few minutes on one core. The number of threads is taken from the job's CPU allocation.
-----
**Citation**
If you use this tool, please cite
Russel J, Pinilla-Redondo R, Mayo-Muñoz D, Shah SA, Sørensen SJ. *CRISPRCasTyper: Automated Identification, Annotation, and Classification of CRISPR-Cas Loci.* The CRISPR Journal (2020). doi:10.1089/crispr.2020.0059
